description:
Barranquilla’s first-ever warehouse rave wasn’t just a party—it was a manifesto. Paria x Siempre Carnaval brought together Caribbean rhythms, global club culture, and queer periphery in an unforgettable night. In the raw glow of the warehouse, the Picó’s mutated, experimental, and futuristic spirit echoed loud.
The event had a clear mission: to fundraise for the Paria Turbo Laser sound system, handmade in Barranquilla by master carpenter César Terán, sound engineer Jaime Álvarez Jr., and visual artist William Gutiérrez. The Picó stands as a collective and political expression: a symbol of grassroots power, underground sound, and Afro‑Caribbean legacy.
